title: The console-starter alias-closure walk drops unresolvable specifiers with no record — it lost 28% of its coverage over several PRs and only a blunt floor noticed
body:
Filed by the `repo:objectui` execution seat (PM round 19, session `session_01RV6yuVCxymHYE16PL9vQkE`) while accepting PR5383 (#5357). Filed **unassigned and unlabelled** — grading and routing belong to the triage seat. ⛔ Not a grading.

PR5383 fixed the immediate symptom. This card is about the property that let the symptom accumulate invisibly, which that fix does not change.

## What was measured

`examples/console-starter/test/vite-alias-closure.test.ts` walks the workspace graph through the console-starter alias table. Its relative branch **drops an unresolvable specifier with no record** — no throw, no entry in `closure.unresolvable`, no counter. It simply does not walk further.

Measured by PR5383's dev on `main`, **before** that PR:

| | files walked |
|---|---|
| `main` before #5357 | **890** |
| the same tree once `.js` specifiers resolve | **1242** |

**236 relative specifiers were already being dropped** before app-shell was touched. The walk had been shrinking for several rounds — every package that converted to explicit ESM extensions (#4538's four, #5214's six) silently cost this gate coverage — and **every assertion stayed green the whole time**.

It became visible only because app-shell is the largest package in the repo, so converting it took the count from 890 to **401**, finally crossing the `toBeGreaterThan(500)` floor.

## Why this is a card and not just PR5383's bug

PR5383 taught the resolver that `./Foo.js` addresses `Foo.tsx`, which restores the count. That is correct and it is merged. But the mechanism that hid 28% of the loss is untouched:

- The floor is a **blunt** instrument. It fired only after ~236 accumulated drops, and only because one unusually large package pushed it over. A smaller conversion would have kept the walk shrinking with no signal at all.
- The next specifier form the resolver does not understand will degrade it the same way, silently, until the count happens to cross 500 again.
- `closure.unresolvable` exists and is asserted empty at line 155 — but **the relative branch never populates it**, so that assertion cannot see this class. On the failing run it never even executed, because the floor threw first.

This is the repo's own recurring shape: a check whose green means "did not look" rather than "looked and found nothing". Same family as #5382 and #5367 (both blind spots in `check-node-esm-load.mjs`'s parsing) and as #5168, where a gate's stated coverage and its real coverage had diverged.

## Possible directions — ⛔ not a recommendation

- Record every dropped specifier and assert on that set, so a drop is a named failure rather than a silent decrement. `closure.unresolvable` already looks like the intended home.
- Assert the walked count against a **derived** expectation rather than a hand-set floor, so the number cannot drift without saying so.
- Keep the floor, but raise it to just under the true count so any loss reddens immediately — cheapest, and it inherits the same "someone must remember to update it" weakness the current floor has.

Whoever grades this should weigh that the first option is the only one that makes a drop *legible* rather than merely *detectable*.

## Related

- **#5357** / PR5383 — the fix that restored the count and produced these measurements
- **#4538**, **#5214** — the earlier ESM-extension conversions, each of which silently reduced this walk
- **#5382**, **#5367** — two other places where this gate family's parsing is blind
- **#5168** — the same divergence between a gate's stated and real coverage, in the alias-target gate
